source: Messier + selected NGC/IC objects; J2000; sizes are major-axis arcmin; distances in light-years

objects.name: Crab Nebula
objects.desc: Remnant of the supernova that blazed in the daytime sky in 1054 AD, powered by a pulsar spinning 30 times a second.
One of the richest globular clusters, about 150,000 stars in a tight ball.
Half a million stars; famous among astronomers for its many variable stars.
The closest globular cluster to Earth, just west of red Antares.
One of the oldest globular clusters, about 13 billion years old.

objects.name: Butterfly Cluster
objects.desc: A bright open cluster whose star pattern resembles a butterfly's wings.

objects.name: Ptolemy's Cluster
objects.desc: A large, bright open cluster known since antiquity, at the tail of Scorpius.

objects.name: Lagoon Nebula
objects.desc: A glowing stellar nursery bisected by a dark lane, visible to the naked eye from dark sites.
A compact globular cluster near the centre of the Galaxy.
A bright globular cluster, a neighbour of M12 in Ophiuchus.

objects.name: Wild Duck Cluster
objects.desc: One of the richest and most compact open clusters, with about 2,900 stars.

objects.name: Gumball Globular
objects.desc: A loose globular cluster that has lost many of its inner stars.

objects.name: Hercules Cluster
objects.desc: The finest globular cluster of the northern sky, with several hundred thousand stars.
A rich globular cluster; a nova was seen in it in 1938.
One of the densest globulars, with a collapsed core and a planetary nebula inside.

objects.name: Eagle Nebula
objects.desc: Home of the Pillars of Creation, towers of gas and dust where stars are forming.

objects.name: Omega Nebula
objects.desc: The Swan or Omega Nebula, one of the brightest star-forming regions in the sky.
A sparse open cluster in the Sagittarius star clouds.
An oblate globular cluster, one of the most flattened known.

objects.name: Trifid Nebula
objects.desc: An emission, reflection and dark nebula divided into three lobes by dust lanes.
A young open cluster only a few million years old, next to the Trifid.

objects.name: Sagittarius Cluster
objects.desc: One of the brightest globular clusters, discovered in 1665.
A rich, bright open cluster of about 150 stars.

objects.name: Sagittarius Star Cloud
objects.desc: A dense patch of the Milky Way through a gap in the dust, seen as a glowing star cloud.
A bright open cluster containing a Cepheid variable star.
A small open cluster with a curious dark void near its centre.

objects.name: Dumbbell Nebula
objects.desc: The first planetary nebula ever discovered, a shell of gas shed by a dying star.
A globular cluster that contains the first millisecond pulsar found in one.
A small cluster of bright stars in the Cygnus Milky Way.
A globular cluster with a dense, collapsed core and a stream of stars.

objects.name: Andromeda Galaxy
objects.desc: The nearest large galaxy and the farthest thing most people can see unaided; it is heading toward the Milky Way.
A compact dwarf elliptical satellite of the Andromeda Galaxy.

objects.name: Triangulum Galaxy
objects.desc: A face-on spiral, the third-largest galaxy of our Local Group; a test of dark-sky quality.
A scattered, bright open cluster that fills a binocular field.
A rich open cluster at the foot of Castor, with fainter NGC 2158 beside it.
The first of three open clusters in Auriga, young and compact.
The richest of the Auriga clusters, with about 500 stars.
A cross-shaped open cluster in Auriga.
A loose naked-eye cluster, best in binoculars.

objects.name: Winnecke 4
objects.desc: A close pair of unrelated stars that Messier took for a nebula.
A bright open cluster just below Sirius, with a ruddy giant at its centre.

objects.name: Orion Nebula
objects.desc: The nearest massive star-forming region and the brightest nebula, visible to the naked eye in Orion's sword.

objects.name: De Mairan's Nebula
objects.desc: A detached part of the Orion Nebula, lit by a single hot star.

objects.name: Beehive Cluster
objects.desc: Praesepe: a bright, nearby open cluster, a naked-eye smudge in Cancer.

objects.name: Pleiades
objects.desc: The Seven Sisters, a bright young cluster wrapped in reflection nebulosity.
A rich cluster with a planetary nebula, NGC 2438, superimposed on it.
A bright, coarse open cluster next to M46.
A large, sparse open cluster in Hydra.
The brightest galaxy of the Virgo Cluster, a giant elliptical.
A heart-shaped open cluster in Monoceros.

objects.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
objects.desc: A grand-design spiral interacting with its companion NGC 5195.
A rich open cluster in Cassiopeia, pointed to by Alpha and Beta Cas.
A distant globular cluster near Alpha Comae Berenices.
A globular cluster that belongs to the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy, not to the Milky Way.
A large, loose globular cluster in southern Sagittarius.
A modest globular cluster midway between Albireo and Gamma Lyrae.

objects.name: Ring Nebula
objects.desc: The classic smoke-ring planetary nebula between Beta and Gamma Lyrae.
A barred spiral in the Virgo Cluster.
An elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster.
A giant elliptical, interacting with the small spiral NGC 4647.
A face-on starburst spiral on the edge of the Virgo Cluster.
A lopsided globular cluster close to the Galactic centre.

objects.name: Sunflower Galaxy
objects.desc: A flocculent spiral with patchy, sunflower-like arms.

objects.name: Black Eye Galaxy
objects.desc: A spiral with a dramatic dark dust lane in front of its bright nucleus.
A spiral in the Leo Triplet.
The brightest of the Leo Triplet, with distorted arms.
One of the oldest known open clusters, about 4 billion years.
A globular cluster in Hydra.
A compact globular cluster in Sagittarius.
A small globular cluster near M69.
A loose cluster once classed as an open cluster, in Sagitta.
A faint, distant globular cluster in Aquarius.
A group of four stars, an asterism rather than a true cluster.

objects.name: Phantom Galaxy
objects.desc: A face-on grand-design spiral, notoriously difficult to see by eye.
A very compact, distant globular cluster.

objects.name: Little Dumbbell Nebula
objects.desc: A faint planetary nebula, the dimmest Messier object.

objects.name: Cetus A
objects.desc: A Seyfert galaxy with a bright, active nucleus.
The brightest reflection nebula in the sky, in Orion.
A globular cluster in Lepus, possibly from a captured dwarf galaxy.
A dense globular cluster between Antares and Beta Scorpii.

objects.name: Bode's Galaxy
objects.desc: A bright grand-design spiral and the anchor of the M81 group.

objects.name: Cigar Galaxy
objects.desc: An edge-on starburst galaxy with streamers of glowing gas blowing from its core.

objects.name: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy
objects.desc: A barred spiral rich in star formation and supernovae.
A lenticular galaxy in Markarian's Chain.
A lenticular galaxy at the northern edge of the Virgo Cluster.
A galaxy approaching us faster than any other in Virgo.

objects.name: Virgo A
objects.desc: A giant elliptical with a famous jet and the first black hole ever imaged.
A bright spiral in the Virgo Cluster.
A round elliptical with faint shells.
A spiral galaxy racing toward us.
A barred spiral, the last of the Virgo objects Messier recorded.
A fine globular cluster in Hercules, often overshadowed by M13.
A bright, wedge-shaped open cluster in Puppis.
A starburst galaxy surrounded by a bright ring.
A barred spiral in the Leo I group.
The brightest spiral of the M96 group in Leo.

objects.name: Owl Nebula
objects.desc: A round planetary nebula with two dark 'eyes'.
A nearly edge-on spiral in Coma Berenices.
A face-on spiral with a lopsided arm pattern.
A grand-design spiral, used to calibrate the Hubble constant.

objects.name: Pinwheel Galaxy
objects.desc: A large, face-on spiral whose outer arms are faint.

objects.name: Spindle Galaxy
objects.desc: An edge-on lenticular galaxy with a sharp dust lane, usually identified with Messier's M102.
A small, triangular open cluster, the last of Messier's own discoveries.

objects.name: Sombrero Galaxy
objects.desc: A spiral with a bright bulge and a prominent dust lane, like a wide-brimmed hat.
An elliptical in the Leo I group.
A spiral with a supermassive black hole and a maser disc used to measure distance.
A loose globular cluster in Ophiuchus.
A nearly edge-on spiral near the Owl Nebula.
A barred spiral near Gamma Ursae Majoris.
A dwarf elliptical satellite of the Andromeda Galaxy.

objects.name: North America Nebula
objects.desc: A huge emission nebula shaped like the North American continent, beside Deneb.

objects.name: Sculptor Galaxy
objects.desc: A dusty starburst spiral, the brightest galaxy in the Sculptor Group.

objects.name: Centaurus A
objects.desc: An elliptical galaxy cut by a dark dust lane, with a powerful radio jet.

objects.name: Carina Nebula
objects.desc: One of the largest and brightest nebulae in the sky, home of the eruptive star Eta Carinae.

objects.name: 47 Tucanae
objects.desc: The second-brightest globular cluster in the sky, beside the Small Magellanic Cloud.

objects.name: Omega Centauri
objects.desc: The largest and brightest globular cluster, probably the core of a stripped dwarf galaxy.

objects.name: Double Cluster
objects.desc: Two young open clusters, NGC 869 and NGC 884, side by side in Perseus.

objects.name: Horsehead Nebula
objects.desc: A dark nebula silhouetted against the glowing hydrogen of IC 434, below Alnitak.

objects.name: Helix Nebula
objects.desc: One of the nearest planetary nebulae, nicknamed the Eye of God.

objects.name: Rosette Nebula
objects.desc: A big circular emission nebula around the young cluster NGC 2244.

objects.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
objects.desc: A satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, a naked-eye cloud in the southern sky.

objects.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
objects.desc: A dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

objects.name: Cat's Eye Nebula
objects.desc: One of the most complex planetary nebulae known, with concentric shells and jets.

objects.name: Needle Galaxy
objects.desc: A beautiful edge-on spiral with a thin dust lane.

objects.name: Silver Sliver Galaxy
objects.desc: An edge-on spiral with a dark dust lane, in Andromeda.

objects.name: Veil Nebula
objects.desc: The Eastern Veil: delicate filaments from a supernova about 10,000 years ago.

objects.name: Tarantula Nebula
objects.desc: The most active star-forming region of the Local Group, inside the Large Magellanic Cloud.

objects.name: Eskimo Nebula
objects.desc: A planetary nebula resembling a face in a fur parka.

objects.name: Crescent Nebula
objects.desc: A shell of gas blown by a Wolf-Rayet star.

objects.name: Flame Nebula
objects.desc: A glowing nebula next to Alnitak, veined with dark dust.

objects.name: California Nebula
objects.desc: A huge, faint hydrogen nebula shaped like the state of California.

objects.name: Elephant's Trunk Nebula
objects.desc: A large emission nebula that contains the dark Elephant's Trunk globule.

objects.name: Southern Pleiades
objects.desc: A bright southern open cluster with the star Theta Carinae.
